description: Two Svelte 5 spreadsheets over two separate documents, kept in step by a delta stream: type in either and the other follows. What crosses the wire is a delta rather than the document, and the log shows each one as it goes. A formula travels as its text, so the other side works out its own answer; an insert travels as the edit, so both sides rewrite their own formulas; a format travels as the one part of the one sheet that changed. Presence rides the same wire and is never part of the document: each window draws the other's selection as a coloured box with a name on it. Conflicts are last writer wins, per cell. A real app puts a socket in the middle with the same onDelta out and apply in. Enterprise, in @svgrid/enterprise.

faq.question: What actually crosses the wire?
faq.answer: A delta of one of five kinds: the raw text of the cells that were written, a structural edit, one part of one sheet's state (the formats, the merges, a rule, the objects), the whole document for adding a sheet and for a first read, or a presence message saying where someone's cursor is. A keystroke is one small message, not a copy of the sheet.

faq.question: Is presence part of the document?
faq.answer: No, and deliberately so. It is a prop on the component and a delta kind that the receiving stream hands to onPresence rather than to the document, so it is never in getState() and never in the .xlsx. A cursor belongs to a session, not to a file.

faq.question: Why send a formula's text rather than its value?
faq.answer: Because the other side has to keep the formula. A collaborator receives =SUM(B2:C2) and their own workbook works out the answer, so the two cannot disagree about a number, and the receiving sheet keeps a formula in the cell rather than a frozen figure.

faq.question: What happens when two people type in the same cell?
faq.answer: Last writer wins, per cell, and both sides converge on whatever arrived last. There is no version vector and no transform: two people in different cells never conflict, which is the case that actually happens, and anything stronger belongs in a different piece of work.
